title: Ten Sentences Term Paper Related to Correlation Analysis in Python & Quatro

Introduction

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

sns.set_context('talk')

df = sns.load_dataset('iris')

For at least five minutes researchers at UW-Madison’s DSHB program have had an interest in learning more about correlations in the iris data from Seaborn. Our program will use this topic as a demonstration of working with correlation analysis in Python and Quarto; we have data from 150 flowers and our research question is to study whether the petel width correlation with pedel length.
Research question: study whether the petal width correlate the petal length


Literature
The data for our analysis was originally published by Unwin and Kleinman (2021). While typically these data are often used to demonstrate classification methods we use it to demonstrate correlation analysis.


Method
Given that we have the column of continuous data with (length of petel and width of petel), we will examine this realtionship by using simple correlation analysis and also a scatterplot. These two methods are classic and traditional starting points when evaluating data like these.


Result

corr_val = np.array(df[['petal_length', 'petal_width']].corr())[0][1]
print(corr_val)

narrative = "a very strong negative correlation"

As shown in the Figure 1 we see additional evidence of a strong positive correlation bewteen a iris flower petal length and petal width.


Discussion
Now that this long-standing problem (of over 10 minutes) is resolved (thanks to the diligent efforts of UW-Madison’s DSHB program) science has once again triumphed in establishing that there is a positive correlative relationship between iris petal width and iris petal length as a matter of empircally certain ground truth.
